land.text: the camp of warriors from Oyo, Ife and Ijebu that became Ibadan in 1829, in the turmoil of the Oyo collapse

predecessors.note: The Ibadan page names Ife, Ijebu and Oyo as the origins of the warriors; the Oyo Empire dossier (af-04-a) dates Oyo-Ile's end to 1835.

land.text: the Ibadan area, a British protectorate after the treaty of 15 August 1893

successors.note: 'In 1893, the Ibadan area became a British Protectorate after a treaty signed by Fijabi, the Baale of Ibadan, with the British acting Governor of Lagos Colony, George C. Denton, on 15 August.'

capitals.name: Ibadan
capitals.note: Gazetteer point for Ibadan (3.928 E, 7.382 N).

correction.text: Ibadan, 'came into existence in 1829', a martial city-state

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no extent and no area; a 40 km circle round Ibadan stands for the city-state and its farms.

correction.text: the Ibadan empire: 'Between the 1860s and 1890s, the city-state became the center of an empire'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page names no tributary town and gives no frontier ('The tributary towns (Ijebu, Ife, Ekiti)' appear only as the origins of the warriors); Oyo, Osun and Ekiti states (about 44,000 km2) are a stand-in for the central Yoruba region; confidence 1.

ledger.note: 1829: Ibadan comes into existence. Ibadan 'came into existence in 1829, during a period of turmoil that characterized Yorubaland at the time'; 'retained its martial character until the last decade of the 19th century'.

region.text: the central Yoruba country round Ibadan, no town named by the page

ledger.note: 1860s: Ibadan becomes the centre of an empire. 'Between the 1860s and 1890s, the city-state became the center of an empire.' The page names no conquests and no year; 1860 is the start of the 1860s.

region.text: the Ibadan area and its dependencies

ledger.note: 1893 (15 August): Ibadan accepts British protection. 'In 1893, the Ibadan area became a British Protectorate after a treaty signed by Fijabi, the Baale of Ibadan' with the acting Governor of Lagos Colony, George C. Denton, on 15 August.
1893 (15 August): Ibadan ceases to be independent; the Baale and the city continue under the protectorate.

wars.name: Ibadan against the Sokoto Caliphate forces
wars.outcome: The Sokoto Caliphate was 'decisively defeated by the armies of Ibadan in 1840' (Ibadan page); no place or land is given.

certainty.note: No frontier is given; the empire is a regional stand-in, the city-state a circle.

sources.title: Ibadan
sources.note: Founded 1829; martial city-state; centre of an empire between the 1860s and 1890s; defeated Sokoto forces in 1840; protectorate treaty of 15 August 1893 with Fijabi, Baale of Ibadan; nothing on the Ijaye War, the Kiriji War or tributary towns.

notes: Ibadan has no Cliopatria row. One page opened (budget 1-2); it does not mention the Ijaye War (1860-62), the Ekitiparapo/Kiriji War (1877-1893) or any tributary town, so the 1860 gain is a confidence-1 stand-in and the Kiriji War is not listed. A gap-filler should open 'Kiriji War' and 'Ijaye'. The Ibadan page is the city's article; the dossier is the state (the Wikipedia title has no separate state page). New Oyo (the Alafin's Oyo from 1835), the Egba United Government and the Ilorin Emirate are separate Yoruba successor states named in the Lagos dossier; they have no dossier here.
